description: A black rook on e8 pins the white knight on e3 to the white king on e1 along the e-file; the knight keeps all its geometric reach at L0 but can exercise none of it at L1, and so no longer defends the pawn on d5.
decisions: Only a pin against the piece's own king is a pin. The pinned piece stays between pinner and king with no other piece on the line between them.
A pinned piece keeps its full L0 reach; every attack off the pin line is excluded at L1 with reason pinned, and the explanation names the pinning piece and its square.
A knight can never move along a line, so a pinned knight has no legal move; its no-legal-moves reason is pinned.
The pinner's line does not continue through the pinned piece as an L0 attack: the rook on e8 does not attack e2 or e1, because a knight is neither a same-line piece (no x-ray) nor the enemy king.
The king is not in check while the pinned piece stands on the line.

assertions.note: At L0 the knight still defends the pawn on d5.
At L1 it does not: moving to d5 would leave the e-file open.
The knight blocks; no x-ray through a knight.
Only the white king reaches e2.
